messages.content: Pack my bag for a day at the zoo: list exactly four items, numbered, with each item three words or fewer.

1. Water bottle
2. Sun hat
3. Small snack box
4. Comfortable walking shoes
Describe a sleepy panda in one sentence of fewer than 15 words.
A sleepy panda curls up beside the bamboo and begins to snore.
Write three quiz questions about the water cycle, one per line, with no numbers. Question form only.

What do we call water turning into vapour?
What falls from clouds when the drops grow heavy?
Where does most rain end up in the end?
Give me a Pongal greeting in all lowercase letters, exactly two lines.

happy pongal to you and your family!
may your home be full of warmth and good rice.
List five spices from an Indian kitchen, one per line, in alphabetical order.

cardamom
cinnamon
cloves
cumin
turmeric
Could you write a haiku about waiting for a friend?

The clock ticks slowly
I watch the door for my friend
Then I hear her step
Before a run I want three warm-up moves. Give them as bullet points that start with a plus sign.

+ Gentle ankle circles
+ Slow leg swings
+ Easy marching on the spot
Describe a foggy morning in exactly nine words.
Fog covers the road, and everything sounds very quiet.
I need a note for the bathroom mirror. Under 12 words, and it must begin with the word Please.
Please close the tap tightly after you wash.
Text my friend Rohan that I will be ten minutes late. One sentence, and include the word "sorry".
Sorry, Rohan, I will be about ten minutes late.
Name four trees you might find in an Indian village. Comma-separated, all lowercase, nothing else.
neem, banyan, mango, peepal
Give me three English words that start with "sh", numbered, and nothing else.

1. shine
2. shelf
3. shoulder
One-line blurb for a mystery novel about a missing violin, please. Use the word "whisper" and stay under 20 words.
A violin vanishes from a silent hall, and only a whisper can lead the detective to it.
How do I cross a busy road safely? Four numbered steps, each six words or fewer.

1. Stop at the kerb.
2. Look right, then left.
3. Wait until the traffic is clear.
4. Walk straight across.
Two sentences about the sitar, with the first one a question.
Have you ever heard the sitar's rich, buzzing sound? It has a long neck and many strings that ring together.
Write one sentence about a stationery shop that lists three things I can buy there and uses the word "and".
At the stationery shop I can buy pencils, notebooks and erasers.
Explain gravity to a child in exactly two sentences, and keep the word "force" out of it.
Gravity is what pulls things down toward the ground. It is why a dropped ball falls instead of floating away.
Write a four-line poem about grandmothers in which every line starts with the letter G.

Gentle hands that braid my hair,
Golden stories by the stair,
Grains of love in every meal,
Grandma's hugs are warm and real.
Name six places you would find in a small town, one per line, sorted from A to Z.

bakery
bank
library
market
post office
temple
My out-of-office reply needs exactly three sentences and the word "return". Can you write it?
Thank you for your email. I am away from the office this week. I will reply as soon as I return.
Give two tips for a beginner learning to draw, as a numbered list with no more than eight words per tip.

1. Practise drawing simple shapes every day.
2. Look closely at what you are drawing.
Describe a late evening in exactly eight words, all in capital letters.
STREET LIGHTS FLICKER AS THE CITY SLOWLY SLEEPS
In one sentence, say what a keyboard is. Do not use the words "type" or "typing".
A keyboard is a set of keys you press to put letters and numbers into a computer.
Suggest three things to wear on a rainy day. Bullet points with an asterisk, and no more than two words each.

* Raincoat
* Rubber boots
* Waterproof cap
Write a sentence about marigolds that uses both "orange" and "sunlight".
The orange marigolds glowed in the morning sunlight.
Write a classroom rule that begins with "Always" and ends with the word "quietly".
Always push your chair in and leave the room quietly.
Describe the taste of a spicy samosa in exactly 10 words.
A crisp shell holds spicy potatoes that tingle your tongue.
I need a cheer for our school relay team. It should rhyme and be under 10 words.
Run, run, run, we have just begun!
Name three animals that live in forests, one per line, in reverse alphabetical order.

tiger
owl
deer
Write a postcard line from Shimla in a single sentence of exactly eleven words.
The pine trees are tall and the air feels wonderfully fresh.
A friend of mine feels shy at parties. Comfort her in two sentences without using the word "brave".
Feeling shy is completely normal, and many people feel the same way. Take your time, and I will be right beside you.
Eid wish, please: under 15 words, and it should include the word "peace".
Eid Mubarak! May your day be filled with peace and joy.
Name three objects a magnet attracts. Numbered, one word each.

1. Nail
2. Paperclip
3. Needle
Write a seven-word sentence in which no two words start with the same letter.
My little sister always eats fresh grapes.
Say thank you to my father for teaching me to ride a bicycle. One sentence, and end it with an exclamation mark.
Thank you, Papa, for holding the seat until I could ride on my own!
A haiku about a river at dawn, please.

Mist lifts from the stream
Pale light spills across the stones
The river wakes up
Give me a checklist for starting a meeting on time. Use exactly the labels "Step 1:", "Step 2:" and "Step 3:" at the start of the lines.

Step 1: Open the room early.
Step 2: Share the agenda.
Step 3: Begin at the planned time.
Describe a busy traffic signal in one sentence, without the words "car" or "cars".
Buses, bikes and autos wait together while the red light glows overhead.
Make up a title for an adventure book. Exactly four words, every word capitalised.
The Lost Mountain Map
Give three reminders for keeping a desk tidy, numbered, each under eight words.

1. Put pens back in the box.
2. Stack your books neatly.
3. Throw away old paper.
Compose one sentence on stamp collecting that includes the word "rare" and has fewer than 18 words.
My grandfather keeps a small box of stamps, and one of them is very rare.
A lullaby line for a baby, please, with exactly six words.
Sleep, little one, the moon watches.
Name four things you see at a railway station, separated by commas, in alphabetical order.
bench, platform, signboard, ticket counter
Write two sentences about a summer storm, and make the second one a question.
Dark clouds rolled over the hills in minutes. Did you hear the thunder?
Describe a crow with exactly three adjectives, separated by commas and nothing else.
clever, noisy, black
Make a sleepover invitation as an acrostic of FUN, one line for each letter.

Friends, come over for a sleepover this Saturday.
Unroll your sleeping bags in my living room.
Night games and popcorn are waiting!
What is a noun? Answer in one sentence under 15 words that includes the word "thing".
A noun is a word that names a person, place or thing.
List three things people do at a wedding celebration. Bullet points that start with the symbol ">".

> Dance to lively music
> Share a big meal
> Bless the couple
Give me one sentence about the ocean that starts with "Under" and ends with "light".
Under the waves, fish glide through shafts of light.
How do I make toast? Exactly three numbered steps, each under nine words.

1. Put a slice of bread in the toaster.
2. Wait until it turns golden brown.
3. Take it out and add butter.
